results.label: SC-29_guardrail_halt_sequential_node
results.assessment: fast-mode claim denied, consistent with the small-claim-deductible pattern - this scenario was meant to test a forced guardrail-budget-halt (needs a config change to trigger for real, same caveat as scenarios1's SC-07), which was not exercised this round

cross_batch_findings: Confirms the SAME structural pattern from scenarios1: most full-fan-out claims pause at or before consistency_coordinator due to damage_assessor.requires_physical_inspection=True, driven by the known missing-document-upload gap - this is not new information, just further confirmation at scale.

SC-08's policy_checker independently flagging a 'staged accident' compliance concern, entirely separate from the mocked fraud_crew, is a genuinely positive finding: a real cross-check caught a real signal even with the fraud detection agent excluded from this round.

Several scenarios specifically designed to test paths AFTER the fan-out (SC-08's auto-reject, SC-14's own target succeeded, SC-17's clean settlement, SC-20's quality gate, SC-23's full completion) could not reach their intended target this round because the physical-inspection trigger fires first in most cases - this means the LIVE-TESTED coverage of 'what happens after settlement' is thinner than the scenario COUNT suggests. The mocked test suite (tests/test_scenarios_e2e.py) still proves these later branches are correctly WIRED; live runs with this particular document-less claim data just can't reach them as often as hoped.
